evSpots.HP: HP Up vitamins; Marill by Surf on the Sevii Islands (+2, post-game), or a +1 like Nidoran♀
evSpots.Atk: Mankey on Route 22 (+1); Machoke / Primeape in Cerulean Cave (+2, post-game)
evSpots.Def: Geodude in Mt. Moon / Rock Tunnel (+1); Graveler in Victory Road (+2)
evSpots.SpA: Gastly in Pokémon Tower (+1, ~90% there); Kadabra / Magneton in Cerulean Cave (+2, post-game)
evSpots.SpD: Tentacool by Surf almost anywhere (+1); Tentacruel (+2)
evSpots.Spe: Diglett in Diglett's Cave (+1); Dugtrio there too (+2)

stops.name: Pallet Town — Starter

items.name: Starter Pokémon
items.why: Bulbasaur trivialises Brock+Misty; Squirtle is the safest all-game pick; Charmander is the hard mode (loses to first two gyms).

items.name: Poké Balls x5
items.why: First catching supply.

items.name: Town Map
items.why: Free, one dialogue.

items.name: Potion
items.why: Free item on the PC in your house.

stops.notes: Route 1 is a level-2 grind lane. Don't over-catch here — Pidgey/Rattata are both available for the rest of Kanto.

stops.name: Viridian City & Route 22

items.name: Poké Balls (Mart)
items.why: Stock ~10 before Viridian Forest.

items.name: TM Bide
items.why: Free, skippable.

stops.notes: Route 22 has Mankey/Spearow/Nidoran — Mankey is the single best early answer to Brock AND Misty's Starmie is neutral to it. Rival battle on Route 22 is optional.

stops.name: Viridian Forest & Route 2

items.name: Antidote / Potion / Poké Ball
items.why: Free consumables on the way through.

stops.notes: Pikachu is here at a low rate (FR/LG ~5%). If you want one, get it now — the next spot is Power Plant, very late.

stops.name: Pewter City — Brock

items.name: TM39 Rock Tomb
items.why: Gym reward.

items.name: Old Amber
items.where: Pewter Museum (needs Cut, come back later)
items.why: Aerodactyl — revive it at Cinnabar Lab.

items.name: Running Shoes
items.why: Straight movement-speed win. Don't skip.

stops.notes: Boulder Badge enables Flash out of battle.

stops.name: Route 3 & Mt. Moon

items.name: Moon Stone x1 (+ hidden ones)
items.why: Only reliable Moon Stone before Celadon. Nidorino→Nidoking or Clefairy→Clefable.

items.name: Dome or Helix Fossil
items.why: One-time exclusive choice. Omanyte (Helix) is the stronger of the two; both need Cinnabar Lab, very late.

items.name: TM12 Water Gun / Rare Candy
items.why: Free.

stops.notes: Mt. Moon is the Zubat/Geodude/Paras pool. Nidoran♂ from Route 3 + the Moon Stone here is the classic power spike.

stops.name: Cerulean City — Misty

items.name: Bike Voucher
items.why: Biggest single playtime-speed item in the game. Get it the moment Route 25 opens.

items.name: TM03 Water Pulse
items.why: Gym reward.

items.name: TM28 Dig
items.where: Cerulean, man behind the Rocket house
items.why: Strong early Ground move; also an escape rope.

items.name: Nugget x1
items.why: Sells for 5000. Fund your Bike-era shopping.

stops.notes: Cascade Badge enables Cut. Abra is on Route 24/25 — catch one, it's a top-3 sweeper (Alakazam) and only needs a trade or level 16.

stops.name: Routes 5–6, Vermilion City

items.name: Bicycle
items.where: Vermilion Bike Shop, with the Voucher
items.why: Do this first thing on arrival.

items.name: Old Rod
items.why: Magikarp → Gyarados. Slow to train, huge payoff.

items.name: Squirtle (trade)
items.why: Free second water type if you skipped it as a starter.

stops.notes: Diglett's Cave connects Route 2 to Route 11 — Diglett/Dugtrio here are the fastest Pokémon in the early game and clean up Surge.

stops.name: S.S. Anne

items.name: HM01 Cut
items.why: Required to leave the ship and to reach the Vermilion Gym.

items.name: TM31 Mega Kick / misc
items.why: Sweep the rooms before you get Cut — the ship vanishes permanently after the gym.

stops.notes: One-time area. Loot everything before you leave; it is gone for the rest of the save.

stops.name: Vermilion City — Lt. Surge

items.name: TM34 Shock Wave
items.why: Gym reward.

items.name: HM05 Flash
items.where: Route 2 east gate via Diglett's Cave (need 10 species caught)
items.why: Rock Tunnel is miserable without it.

items.name: Itemfinder
items.why: Optional.

stops.notes: Thunder Badge enables Fly — but you don't get HM02 until Route 16. Dugtrio or any Ground type walks the gym.

stops.name: Routes 9–10 & Rock Tunnel

items.name: TM43 Secret Power / Elixir
items.why: Free.

stops.notes: Needs Cut to enter Route 9. Bring Flash. The Power Plant is visible from Route 10 but is unreachable until you have Surf — it shows up under Fuchsia.

stops.name: Lavender Town & Routes 7–8
stops.notes: Pokémon Tower is blocked until you have the Silph Scope from the Celadon Rocket Hideout. Pass straight through to Celadon.

stops.name: Celadon City — Erika, Game Corner, Rocket Hideout

items.name: Eevee
items.why: Free. Vaporeon/Jolteon/Flareon — Vaporeon is the strongest of the three for the rest of the run.

items.name: Evolution stones (Dept. Store 4F)
items.why: Fire/Water/Thunder/Leaf Stone for sale. This is the evolution-timing checkpoint for Eevee, Pikachu, Gloom, Growlithe, Vulpix, Staryu, Shellder, Exeggcute.

items.name: Vitamins (Protein, Carbos, HP Up...)
items.why: Vitamins (Protein/Carbos etc.) are the cheapest permanent stat boost — buy for your two carries.

items.name: Silph Scope
items.why: Hard gate for Pokémon Tower.

items.name: Coin Case + Game Corner prizes
items.why: Porygon / Dratini / Scyther / Pinsir here. Dratini is a long-term Dragonite; the coin grind is real playtime cost — buy coins, don't spin.

items.name: TM19 Giga Drain
items.why: Gym reward.

stops.notes: Rainbow Badge enables Strength (you get HM04 later, at Fuchsia). Celadon is the single biggest decision node in the game — stones, Eevee, Game Corner, vitamins all land here.

stops.name: Pokémon Tower

items.name: Poké Flute
items.where: Mr. Fuji, after clearing the Tower
items.why: Wakes the two Snorlax and unblocks Routes 12 and 16.

stops.notes: Gastly/Haunter here. Haunter → Gengar needs a trade; without one, Haunter still hits hard. Marowak on 6F is a scripted un-catchable fight.

stops.name: Routes 12–18, Cycling Road, Snorlax

items.name: HM02 Fly
items.why: Second-biggest playtime-speed item after the Bike. Teach it immediately.

items.name: Super Rod
items.why: Opens the real water encounter pool.

items.name: Snorlax x2
items.why: One-time each, level 30, huge bulk. Save before engaging.

items.name: TM13 Ice Beam / Exp. Share
items.where: Route 12 floor / Route 15 Oak's Aide (50 species)
items.why: Exp. Share is a big grind reducer for a sixth-slot carry.

stops.notes: With Fly + Bike, backtracking cost drops to near zero. This is the point to sweep every skipped item.

stops.name: Fuchsia City — Koga & Safari Zone

items.name: HM03 Surf
items.why: Opens roughly a third of the map. Highest-priority item in this stop.

items.name: Gold Teeth → HM04 Strength
items.where: Safari Zone Area 3, then the Warden
items.why: Required for Victory Road and Seafoam.

items.name: TM06 Toxic
items.why: Gym reward.

items.name: Good Rod
items.why: Minor.

items.name: Chansey / Kangaskhan / Scyther / Pinsir / Tauros / Dratini
items.why: Tauros and Kangaskhan are the best combat picks here; Chansey is an Exp piñata.

stops.notes: Soul Badge enables Surf. Safari Zone is step-limited — decide what you want before entering, don't wander. Surf also opens the Power Plant off Route 10 — Electabuzz, Voltorb and Zapdos, and the best Electric answer you'll get before the League.

stops.name: Saffron City — Silph Co. & Sabrina

items.name: Lapras
items.where: Silph Co. 7F, free from an employee
items.why: Free, one-time, excellent Water/Ice. Take it.

items.name: Master Ball
items.why: Save it for Mewtwo or a roamer.

items.name: Hitmonlee or Hitmonchan
items.why: One-time exclusive choice. Hitmonlee's higher Attack/Speed makes it the better pick in FRLG.

items.name: TM04 Calm Mind
items.why: Gym reward.

stops.notes: Marsh Badge enables Rock Smash. Sabrina is the hardest gym — bring a Bug, Ghost or Dark option; a Gengar or Snorlax with Bite/Crunch is the practical answer.

stops.name: Routes 19–21 & Seafoam Islands

items.name: Articuno
items.why: Level 50 legendary, one-time. Save first.

stops.notes: Surf opens the entire southern sea. Tentacool/Krabby/Horsea pools are here.

stops.name: Cinnabar Island — Pokémon Mansion & Blaine

items.name: Secret Key
items.why: Hard gate for the gym.

items.name: Fossil revivals
items.why: Cash in Helix/Dome/Old Amber here — Kabutops/Omastar/Aerodactyl arrive at level 5, so only worth it if you'll actually train one.

items.name: Electrode/Magmar
items.why: Magmar is a solid late Fire type if you never picked Charmander.

items.name: TM38 Fire Blast
items.why: Gym reward.

stops.notes: Volcano Badge enables Waterfall. Bill meets you outside the gym afterwards — that starts the Sevii Islands leg.

stops.name: Sevii Islands 1–3 (story leg)

items.name: HM06 Rock Smash
items.why: Needed for Sevii traversal.

items.name: Ruby
items.why: Celio's network machine — this is the story gate.

items.name: Moltres
items.why: Level 50 legendary, one-time.

items.name: Rescue Lostelle
items.why: Story gate — the Hypno fight.

stops.notes: Bill hands you the Tri-Pass after Blaine. This leg is mandatory story, not optional — clear it before heading back to Viridian.

stops.name: Viridian City — Giovanni

items.name: TM26 Earthquake
items.why: Best physical Ground move in the game — teach it to your bulkiest hitter before the Elite Four.

stops.notes: Eighth badge. Grass and Water types walk this gym.

stops.name: Route 23 & Victory Road

items.name: Zapdos
items.where: Power Plant — reachable by Surf from Route 10
items.why: Last legendary before the E4; also the best answer to Lorelei and Lance.

items.name: Rare Candy / Max Elixir / TM17 Protect
items.why: Free.

stops.notes: Needs Strength, Surf and Rock Smash. Last chance to shop — buy 20+ Hyper Potions and a stack of Full Restores before entering the League.

stops.name: Indigo Plateau — Elite Four & Champion
stops.notes: Lorelei (Ice) → Bruno (Fighting) → Agatha (Ghost/Poison) → Lance (Dragon/Flying) → Rival. No healing between fights: an Electric or Rock type covers Lorelei and Lance, a Psychic covers Bruno, and Agatha is the reason to carry a Ground or Psychic move. Recommended party floor: level 55.

stops.name: Post-game — National Dex, Sevii 4–7, Cerulean Cave

items.name: HM07 Waterfall
items.why: Opens the last of the map.

items.name: Mewtwo
items.why: Level 70. This is what the Master Ball was for.

items.name: Ruby + Sapphire → National Dex
items.where: Sapphire is in the Rocket Warehouse, Five Island
items.why: Unlocks Gen 2 Pokémon in the Sevii Islands and the Rainbow Pass.

stops.notes: Everything here is optional. Sevii 4–7 is where the Gen 2 encounters live after the National Dex.

dexBlockers.note: You keep one starter for the whole run. The other two lines — 6 dex entries — only ever arrive by trade.
Helix or Dome, never both. Whichever you leave costs you 2 entries.
The Fighting Dojo gives you exactly one.
Distribution events and the Aurora/Mystic Ticket. Not obtainable in normal play.

catalogue.name: TM05 Roar
catalogue.where: Outside Mt. Moon; Celadon Dept. Store

catalogue.name: TM33 Reflect
catalogue.where: S.S. Anne B1F; Celadon Dept. Store roof

catalogue.name: HM04 Strength
catalogue.where: Fuchsia Warden, for the Gold Teeth

npcs.name: Move Relearner (Move Maniac)
npcs.where: Two Island — purple-roofed house by the Pokémon Center
npcs.why: Re-teaches any move the Pokémon should have learnt by level-up and missed. Costs 2 TinyMushrooms or 1 Big Mushroom — both are held items on wild Paras and Parasect.

npcs.name: Move Deleter
npcs.where: Fuchsia City — house next to the Pokémon Center
npcs.why: The only way to remove an HM move. Nothing else can overwrite Cut, Fly, Surf, Strength, Flash, Rock Smash or Waterfall.

npcs.name: Starter ultimate move tutor
npcs.why: Teaches Frenzy Plant / Hydro Cannon / Blast Burn — once each, to a fully evolved Venusaur, Blastoise or Charizard only.
